items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the highway law, in relation to designating a portion of the state highway system as the "Captain John J. Levulis Memorial Highway"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5854

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the highway law, in relation to designating a portion
of the state highway system as the "Captain John J. Levulis Memorial
Highway"

 PURPOSE :

To designate a portion of state route 75 in the county of Erie as the
"Captain John J. Levulis Memorial Highway."

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1. Amends the highway law to designate the portion of state
route 75 that runs from the Hamburg and Eden town line, in a generally
southerly direction, to the Eden and North Collins town line as the
"Captain John J. Levulis Memorial Highway."

Section 2. Provides for the signing and maintenance of this
designation, and provides that this designation is of a ceremonial
nature and does not change the official name of state route 75.

Section 3. Provides that this act shall take effect immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This designation serves to honor the memory of Captain John J.
Levulis, a member of the United States Army, who tragically lost his
life on May 7, 2015, as a result of injuries suffered in a crash on
the New Jersey Turnpike. Captain Levulis was traveling with three
other soldiers in a Humvee, as part of a convoy en route to Fort Dix.

New York State Route 75 runs through Captain Levulis' hometown of
Eden, where he was an active and beloved member of the community.
This designation will be a fitting tribute to Captain Levulis'
enduring legacy in the Town of Eden, and a comforting reminder for his
friends and family of his sacrifice and courage. Naming a portion of
this highway after this fallen hero is symbolic of the immense
gratitude and pride felt by the Town of Eden, the State of New York,
and the United States of America for Captain John J Levulis.

Captain Levulis was a summa cum laude graduate of Niagara University,
a ROTC cadet, and a graduate of Eden High School, where he played both
basketball and lacrosse. As an illustration of his patriotism at an
early age, he built a Veterans Memorial in front of an American
Legion, for his Eagle Scout project. After graduating college, he
served a tour of duty in Afghanistan, where he held the position of
Infantry Platoon Leader with the 10th Mountain Division, stationed at
Fort Drum.

Captain Levulis was the recipient of numerous awards and accolades
including the Bronze Star, Combat Infantry Badge, Afghanistan campaign
medal, NATO campaign medal, Airborne Wings, and the Meritorious
Service medal. As his family and friends will always remember, he
lived by the credo of "Do your best. Work hard. Be respectful. Show
up. Do the right thing, and sometimes, 'Kwitcher bellyaching.'"

We must never forget the courage and sacrifice made by this country's
veterans, and in so many ways, Captain Levulis is emblematic of what
makes the United States a great nation. He was a true patriot, and his
heroism is an inspiration to all those who had the good fortune to
know him. He will always be remembered.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
